title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Deployment, Packaging, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade and Rollback
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Overview

This document is a consolidated deployment and operations reference for Redwood Inference private deployments: VPC-hosted private control plane installs and fully on-prem packaged deployments. It covers reference architectures, packaging and install artifacts, pre-deployment requirements, step-by-step deployment procedures, day-2 operations, and upgrade & rollback procedures. Use this doc when preparing customer engagements, handoffs to Solutions Engineering, or writing customer SOWs.

Scope and audience

- Scope: VPC-based private control plane, on-prem (air-gapped and connected) packaging, general network/security requirements, day-2 runbooks, and upgrade/rollback playbooks.
- Audience: Solutions Engineers, Platform/Infra Engineers, Customer Site Reliability Engineers, Professional Services.

High-level goals

- Safe, repeatable deployment patterns for VPC and on-prem customers.
- Clear day-2 operational guidance (monitoring, backups, scaling).
- Deterministic upgrade & rollback steps that minimize customer downtime.

Reference architectures (summary)

1) VPC-hosted private control plane (recommended for most enterprise customers)

- Components: redwood-control-plane (managed control plane components), inference-runtime (Kubernetes DaemonSet / Deployment), model-store (S3-compatible object store), redis-kv-cache (optional for prefix caching), metrics pipeline (otel-collector -> prometheus -> grafana), ingress (NGINX or ALB), external DB (managed RDS/Postgres for metadata), KMS/HSM integration for keys.
- Network: Private subnets for inference nodes, public subnets for control-plane egress (if required), VPC endpoints for S3-compatible object store, strict security groups restricting only necessary ports (see Network & Security Requirements).
- Sizing guidance: 1 GPU node per 6-10 q4-like small latency workers depending on model size (see Hardware recommendations).

2) On-prem (air-gapped) packaged deployment

- Components packaged as OCI images in an on-prem registry (Harbor/Artifactory) and a Helm chart that supports offline installation. Include pre-seeded model bundles or on-site model-sync job to pull from customer-approved model registry.
- Hardware: Dedicated GPU hosts (NVidia A100/H100 or equivalent), local object store (minio) recommended for model artifacts.
- Management: Optional Satellite control plane that periodically syncs usage data (when permitted).

Network & security requirements (minimum)

- Required ports (example):
  - 443 (control-plane API egress from customer admin nodes, optional)
  - 80/443 (ingress to inference endpoints behind LB)
  - 9090 (Prometheus metrics, internal only)
  - 9100 (node-exporter)
  - 2379/2380 (etcd cluster - internal cluster only)
  - 10250 (kubelet API - internal)
- Security controls: RBAC for kubernetes, pod security policies/OPA/Gatekeeper, network policies default deny with explicit allow lists, TLS mutual auth on internal service-to-service traffic, KMS/HSM integration for model encryption keys.
- Audit & logging: Fluentd/Vector forwarding to customer SIEM; retention SLA configurable (default 90 days).

Packaging & install artifacts

- Deliverables for on-prem installs:
  - Helm chart tarball (redwood-private-helm-<version>.tgz)
  - OCI image bundle or registry mirror instructions (images.txt with digests)
  - Installation manifest templates (values-vpc.yaml, values-onprem.yaml)
  - Offline dependencies archive (cncf-helm-bundle.tar.gz) for air-gapped installs
  - Seeded model bundles (optional) and model-sync job YAML
- Recommended distribution: SHA256-signed release artifacts + signed SBOM.

Pre-deployment checklist (customer readiness)

1) Networking & identity
  - Customer has dedicated VPC/subnet ranges and route tables provided.
  - Firewall rules opened per Network & Security Requirements above.
  - DNS entries for control-plane and inference endpoints.
  - Service account/role mappings for control-plane components.
2) Storage & secrets
  - S3-compatible endpoint (URL, credentials), or local MinIO configured.
  - KMS/HSM integration details (endpoint, key IDs, access policies).
3) Compute & capacity
  - GPU inventory and rack-level network topology documented.
  - Node OS baseline (Ubuntu 22.04 or RHEL 8.x), NVIDIA driver versions verified.
4) Compliance & access
  - SOC2/Pen test attestation required (if restricted).
  - Emergency access (break-glass) and on-call roster provided.

Deployment procedure (VPC-control plane) - canonical flow

1) Prepare control plane
  - Provision network and managed Postgres (RDS).
  - Apply DNS and obtain TLS certs (ACME or customer-provided certs).
  - Deploy redwood-control-plane helm release:

    kubectl create ns redwood-control
    helm repo add redwood https://charts.redwood.ai/stable
    helm install redwood-control redwood/redwood-control --namespace redwood-control -f values-vpc.yaml

  - Verify control-plane health: 3/3 control-plane pods Running, health endpoint /healthz returns 200.

2) Deploy inference runtime
  - Prepare node labels for GPU scheduling (node.kubernetes.io/gpu=true).
  - Install inference-runtime chart:

    helm install inference-runtime redwood/inference-runtime -n redwood-runtime -f values-runtime.yaml

  - Post-deploy checks: verify inference-runtime pods are Ready, check GPU drivers with nvidia-smi, validate model-store connectivity.

3) Smoke tests and baseline SLO verification
  - Run quick load test (k6 or wrk) with a sample prompt set. Expected baseline: p95 token-latency <= 200ms for short seq (<=256 tokens) on recommended hardware; error rate < 0.1%.

Deployment procedure (on-prem air-gapped) - canonical flow

1) Registry & artifact provisioning
  - Mirror OCI images to customer registry per images.txt using skopeo sync or docker registry mirror.
  - Distribute Helm tarball and offline bundle to customer.
2) Installation steps
  - Load Helm chart and dependency artifacts to the cluster control plane: helm install --dependency-update redwood-private-helm-<version>.tgz -n redwood
  - Apply offline CRDs and operator manifests first.
  - Run model-sync job to pre-seed critical model artifacts.

Day-2 operations (runbooks & monitoring)

Monitoring & dashboards
- Required stack: otel-collector -> prometheus -> grafana. Default dashboards provided: inference latency, token throughput, model cache hit rate, GPU utilization, per-route cost breakdown.
- Key alert thresholds (defaults, adjustable per customer):
  - Inference error rate > 0.5% for 5m -> P1 alert to on-call.
  - GPU utilization > 92% sustained for 10m -> P2 (capacity planning).
  - Model-store latency > 500ms for 3m -> P1.
  - Control-plane API 5xx rate > 0.2% -> P1.

Backups & disaster recovery
- Metadata DB: daily logical backups retained 30 days; point-in-time recovery enabled where supported.
- Model artifacts: versioned object storage with lifecycle rules; keep last 3 production model versions by default.
- Control-plane config: export Helm values and Kubernetes manifests after every change to an off-cluster Git (customer-managed).

Scaling & autoscaling
- Horizontal scaling of inference replicas via HPA based on custom metric (inference_rps_per_pod). GPU autoscaling: cluster-autoscaler with labels to identify GPU node pools.
- Target GPU utilization: 65-85% under steady state. Avoid sustained >90%.

Maintenance & housekeeping
- Log rotation: filebeat/vector to central logging; rotate logs daily with 7-day local retention.
- Disk pressure: alert when inode or disk usage > 80%. Evict pods if necessary using pre-defined node taints.

Upgrade & rollback procedure (safe path)

Principles
- All upgrades must be tested in a staging environment that mirrors customer infra.
- Use canary or blue/green deploys where possible.
- Always have a tested rollback artifact (previous Helm chart + image digests).

Canary upgrade (recommended for low-risk changes)
1) Create canary release with 5% traffic routing to new revision for 1 hour.
2) Monitor key metrics: error rate, latency p95/p99, GPU OOMs, model cache hit rate.
3) If metrics stable (error increase <0.1 percentage point, latency p95 increase <15%), gradually increase to 25% then 100% over scheduled windows.
4) If any critical alert triggers, initiate rollback immediately (see rollback steps).

Blue/green upgrade (recommended for disruptive changes)
1) Deploy new release to green environment (separate namespace or cluster).
2) Run health checks and smoke tests.
3) Cut traffic to green using load balancer swap or DNS change with low TTL.
4) Keep blue environment for at least 60 minutes as a rollback target.

Rollback steps (immediate)
1) Identify release to rollback to (helm history + stable digest).
2) Scale down new replicas and scale up previous revision: helm rollback <release> <revision> -n <ns>.
3) If deployment replaced underlying images, reapply previous image digests to chart values and helm upgrade.
4) Validate recovery: health endpoints 200, error rate returns to baseline within 5 minutes, check model-store connectivity.
5) Post-incident: capture root cause, generate postmortem, and notify stakeholders.

Customer requirements library (common asks and implications)

- Requirement: On-prem air-gapped install with no outbound connectivity
  - Implication: Full offline bundle; customer must mirror OCI images and provide local object store; support windows require PS scripts for Windows hosts.
- Requirement: FIPS-compliant crypto and HSM-backed keys
  - Implication: Enable FIPS mode in control-plane; integrate with customer HSM via PKCS#11. Additional certification and testing may be required.
- Requirement: Long-term model artifact retention (>=365 days)
  - Implication: Adjust lifecycle rules in object store; increase storage SLA and budget.
- Requirement: Strict network egress controls + private connectivity to customer KMS
  - Implication: Use VPC endpoints, private links, and ensure control-plane egress through approved NAT/proxies.

Ownership & escalation

- Default owners:
  - Solutions Engineering: pre-sales deployment validation and initial install assistance.
  - Customer Success/PS: coordinate SOW, runbooks handoff, training.
  - Platform Engineering: post-deploy operational support and critical upgrade execution.
- On-call escalation path (example): Tier 1 -> solutions-eng oncall -> platform eng oncall -> eng-sre -> product-ops lead.

Runbook snippets (examples)

- Quick health check (one-liner):
  kubectl get pods -n redwood-runtime -o wide

- Verify control-plane:
  curl -k https://control-plane.internal.redwood.local/healthz

- Re-seed model cache (if cache stale):
  kubectl apply -f model-sync-job.yaml -n redwood-admin

Appendix A - Hardware recommendations

- Small (POC): 1-2 x A10/A30, 256GB RAM, 10G NIC.
- Production (recommended): 4+ x A100 40GB or H100 80GB per availability domain, NVMe local scratch for model shard caching, 25G/100G network depending on throughput.
- GPU driver: NVIDIA driver 535.x+ (verify compatibility with CUDA 12+).

Appendix B - Example values snippet (Helm)

values-runtime.yaml example:

replicaCount: 3
image:
  repository: registry.local/redwood/inference-runtime
  tag: 2026.02.10
resources:
  requests:
    cpu: "2000m"
    memory: "12Gi"
  limits:
    cpu: "4000m"
    memory: "24Gi"
nodeSelector:
  node.kubernetes.io/gpu: "true"

Appendix C - Test & validation checklist

- Functional: run sample prompt sets and compare outputs to control baseline.
- Performance: p95 latency baseline test, throughput sustained test for 1 hour at target qps.
- Security: run vulnerability scan of images, verify RBAC and network policies.
